review_summary: The repair fixes the prior MEDIUM defect, and I found no new defect in the diff or the focused test. The change is in `QueueStore.request` (`factory-reporting-queue.py:174-177`). Cache admission is now an `if` instead of a `require`. When the cache already holds 128 entries, or admitting the object would pass 32MiB cached, the response is not stored. The code still returns `json.loads(encoded)`, a canonical copy, so callers can't alias the cache. Before that point, the call is already charged against `self.calls < 128`. The size is already charged against `self.consumed <= 32MiB`. The per-response `MAX_STATE*2` check also runs before the admission decision. So a non-admitted read has the same per-operation budgets and validation as before the cache existed. The 128-entry and 32MiB cache caps stay as lifetime caps and are not raised. A hit before the call-bound check still costs no call or bytes. A cached proof stays usable after the cache fills. The test discriminates the fix: the `SequentialReads` subclass (test lines 66-80) does two `read()` calls of 128 unique trees each. The first fills the cache. The second would have raised under the old code. It now passes with 256 provider calls, 128 charged per operation, the cache still at 128 entries and `cached_bytes` within bound. The test then confirms an old entry is still a free hit (no new provider call, `calls` and `consumed` stay 0) and that an uncached object is fetched twice. The other prior findings are addressed. Foreign and prefix-confusion paths now run on fresh adapters, for both DeliveryAPI and QueueStore. Each asserts the exact error and that no provider call was made. A present non-archive `state_view` is asserted to be rejected at construction. Negative regex cases are added: uppercase hex, 39 and 41 characters, a trailing slash, an `/extra` suffix, `git/tags` and `git/refs`. This verdict covers only the cache admission repair and its focused test. It makes no claim about native App or cadence readiness. I did not run the tests.
limitations: Static review only. I executed nothing and did not run the test script. Plan mode was active and the working directory was not a git repository, so my only inputs were the supplied excerpts and diff.

factory-git-state.py was not supplied. I rely on your statement that `state_view_config` rejects any present non-archive config. The test asserts the exact message 'protected state view configuration invalid', and I could not check that string. I also couldn't check whether the approval_path fixture file must exist for construction.
The DeliveryAPI class body was not supplied, so I did not check the 'queue delivery foreign API' message or that class's call and byte accounting. I rely on your report that those checks pass.

The 32MiB cached-bytes admission branch (`self.cached_bytes+size <= 33554432`) has no dedicated test. Only the 128-entry branch is exercised. Both conditions sit in the same `if`, so the fallback is correct by inspection, but a byte-cap regression would not be caught.

I did not re-review the earlier DeliveryAPI redundant-bound nit. It is unchanged, harmless and outside this repair. I did not verify the README matrix claims (real Git, RoutedAPI, CAS, recovery) or the provider-call headroom against the 512 limit, and I infer nothing about native or cadence readiness.
